item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli police have detained ten settlers suspected of attacking a US photographer, a French mayor and other civilians in the West Bank, torching cars and olive trees and wounding farmers. UNICEF reports that 340 children have been killed in Gaza despite a ceasefire. Israeli fire has killed four people in Gaza, according to medics. The Israeli military says a senior Hamas security officer was killed in an airstrike. Half a million Palestinians have lost food aid, according to a humanitarian report. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran has stepped up its maritime attacks, targeting container ships and a tug in the Strait of Hormuz and firing missiles near the UAE, while the IRGC has carried out drone and artillery strikes in Iraqi Kurdistan after a new defence minister was appointed. Lavrov visited Tehran and publicly backed Iran, raising questions about Moscow’s role in the conflict. Houthi forces have continued striking Yemeni army and government training camps, killing dozens of recruits in Shabwa and other locations. Pakistan has halted border trade with Iran following cross-border violence. 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthis have intensified strikes in Yemen, killing 53 soldiers in a training camp and raising the death toll from a later strike on a government camp to 73, the highest single loss since the war resumed. A missile hit a residential area in Taiz, killing two teenage girls, and Houthis attacked a besieged city that the UN says is at grave risk. Saudi Arabia is preparing defensive measures, including deploying Typhoon fighter jets to protect its territory against further Houthi attacks, and the coalition has destroyed a launcher used to target Riyadh. The conflict produced 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Turkish forces are remaining in Syria and Iraq until border security is assured, while the Syrian defence minister reiterates the deployment. DNA testing has identified the remains of seven family members, offering hope to families of the missing, and 600 displaced Syrian families are preparing to return home. The US special envoy praised General Mazloum Abdi for integrating Syrian military units, and the Syrian court continues trials of three defendants in transitional-justice cases. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Ethiopian forces have installed a caretaker administration in Tigray and are moving toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it seized the regional airport and reports Eritrean forces suffered losses there. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the fighting. Mekelle mayor Shishay Amare announced elections will be held within six months and that Western Tigray will be settled through constitutional processes. A drone strike in the disputed Abyei region killed at least 73 people, and the TPLF claims to have killed 1,511 Ethiopian soldiers in recent fighting. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Islamic State-affiliated militants attacked civilians in Mali's Menaka region, killing dozens of people. Mali's military and allied armed groups are also committing abuses against civilians. The conflict remains concentrated in the Sahel, especially Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, where fighting has persisted since 2012. The latest massacre adds to a pattern of jihadist attacks on non-combatants. The war caused 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt: the situation
item.description:
Armed men shot a Kuki civilian in Kangpokpi and villagers were killed in Khongbal Tangkhul, sparking protests in Manipur where effigies of the chief minister and deputy chief minister were burned and bodies of killed civilians were placed outside the chief minister’s residence, prompting calls for resignations. Police arrested multiple suspects in Manipur, seizing firearms and explosives after attacks in Nongshum, Khongban Sanurok and a recent ambush in Kangpokpi, and detained three individuals during a combing operation in Kangpokpi. In Kashmir, the Northern Army commander reviewed security and operational preparedness while buses bound for the region were attacked in Punjab and Haryana, with passengers labeled terrorists. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Philippines: the situation
item.description:
Chinese warships and coast guard vessels continued to monitor a U.S. warship near a disputed shoal while also operating near the Pratas Islands and Scarborough Shoal, prompting the Philippines to summon China’s ambassador over threatening remarks. Vice Admiral Rommel Supangan assumed command of the Philippine Coast Guard and led a rescue of four people, including a child, on Hagonoy Island, Surigao del Sur. Taiwan’s coast guard and maritime forces repelled sixteen mainland Chinese ships near the Pratas Islands. The United States and the Philippines conducted their sixteenth bilateral maritime exercise in the West Philippine Sea. There were 176 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Mexico's cartel violence: the situation
item.description:
Mexican authorities have arrested five suspects linked to the Vizsla silver mining murders, including a man known as El Talibán, and added another Amarillo man to a federal weapons conspiracy case involving the Sinaloa Cartel. An Arizona man killed a dentist in Nogales over bad work and was later killed in a shootout with Mexican police, while a separate Arizona child murder suspect was detained in Mexico after a decade on the run. Journalists continue to be targeted, with 169 murders recorded over 20 years, the longest peacetime wave, according to RSF. Ukrainian-origin fiber-optic drones are being investigated for use by Mexican cartels, prompting FAA restrictions on border drones. 37 battle-related deaths in 1996, according to UCDP.

The United States has lifted sanctions on the leader of Venezuela's National Assembly and deployed Space Force electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against the country. President Nicolás Maduro and his wife face a delayed U.S. torture conspiracy trial scheduled for 2027. A Dutch security report warns that Venezuela's instability could threaten Curaçao and the wider Caribbean Kingdom. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Ukraine has begun using drones to airlift wounded soldiers from the front line, a first operational use of this method. Russian drones have struck Yandex data centres, disrupting Russian court hearings, and have also hit a Kyiv hospital, injuring five people. NATO has increased its Black Sea deployment as Russian attacks intensify, while Poland is seeking an explanation from Ukraine over a drone incident that occurred in Lithuania. The conflict has caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese army is conducting drone strikes on civilian sites, including a market in Abyei where more than 150 people were killed, a mourners' gathering and a fuel market where over 300 were killed, and a market in southern Sudan with hundreds of casualties. The Rapid Support Forces are also using drones to hit economic targets such as gold-mining areas in West Kordofan and near the Egypt border, causing dozens of civilian deaths. These attacks extend drone use from combatant targets to markets, mourners and economic sites, expanding civilian exposure to aerial strikes. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen in Plateau killed NSCDC officer Distu Garba Audu and abducted a businessman, while separate attacks on herders in the same state left two dead and six injured. In Kaduna, bandits abducted five people, including a one-month-old baby, and a fisherman reported his fingers were cut off. Police freed a Catholic priest and seven other abductees in Benue, and bandits killed three policemen on duty in Zamfara. Islamist jihadists burned an evangelist alive in Adamawa, kidnapped a Catholic priest in Benue and struck bases. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

A dispute over the Zangali checkpost is disrupting operations at the Torkham crossing, adding to a broader toll on trade with both Iran and Afghanistan. Pakistan is seeking broader security partnerships, moving to ratify a defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey that expands cooperation beyond bilateral frameworks. The UCDP recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Southern Thailand: the situation
item.description:
Violent attacks persisted in the insurgency zone, with pipe bombs wounding army officers and security volunteers in Narathiwat and Yala and grenade attacks in Trang leading to arrests and seizure of explosives. A Chinese suspect was detained in Bangkok after attempting a 100,000 baht border crossing, and Malaysia appointed a new facilitator for southern Thailand peace talks. Cambodia and Thailand agreed on confidence-building measures at a UNCLOS meeting and discussed easing maritime border tensions, while the WTO and multilateral partners reviewed progress on a supply-chain finance initiative. Floods in Thailand killed 80 people as waters receded, and there were 35 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

European and Ecuadorian police cooperation produced 20 arrests in a major drug-trafficking bust, and nightly curfews were imposed across Ecuador from November 1 to 10 under a state of emergency. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2019, according to UCDP.

Iran-backed Iraqi militias have pledged to defend Iran if attacked, while Iraqi authorities are pursuing legal action against media incitement supporting pro-Iran armed groups and have arrested a lawyer who brandished a gun in court. The Shingal mayoral post, vacant for nine years, is now open for nominations, and Jordan's king reaffirmed support for regional sovereignty and security. item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Fitgharan forces now hold the Mogadishu-Baidoa corridor while Laftagareen forces have seized Buurhakaba and another town in the Bay region, expanding fighting in southern Somalia. Al Shabaab detonated an IED in Mandera, injuring six civilians, and the ICRC treated 148 wounded after heavy combat in Baidoa. Ethiopia announced the withdrawal of more than 3,000 troops from Somalia as its own civil war intensifies, and Ethiopia has refused to intervene in the South West State conflict. Somaliland and Puntland were designated as "friendly" in an Israeli security framework, and Somalia is screening travelers after Kenya confirmed an imported Ebola case and has agreed to acquire Pakistani JF‑17 fighter jets. The UCDP recorded 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

The United Nations renewed sanctions on Haiti and allocated US$75 million for life-saving aid to 507,000 people. Four soldiers are missing after a gang attack and five Salvadoran soldiers disappeared following an ambush, indicating ongoing threats to foreign troops. Elections remain on hold as gangs adapt to the security crackdown, and 193 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Boko Haram is rebuilding its ranks by training about 8,000 children as new fighters, while women farmers in Gella have resisted the group to rebuild a community. Cameroon is pursuing drones and joint border patrols to secure the Nigeria-Cameroon frontier and has offered the Zina and Makary oil blocks to investors after a twelve-year halt. The conflict caused 231 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
